findings.reason: updateSchedule places readSchedulesFile(true), the synchronous callback and writeSchedulesFile inside the existing per-instance writeMetadata queue. No new owner/queue/global reentrancy is introduced. Missing rows/null callbacks do not write; changed identity throws; read/callback/write errors propagate and the existing queue catch keeps later writes usable.

Only timestamp completion, resetConsecutiveFailures and incrementConsecutiveFailures switch to atomic update. They derive their postimage from the latest queued record. Public create/update/pause/resume/delete and execution lifecycle bodies are unchanged.

Automatic pause uses the latest count and threshold; cron pause, warm-up cancellation and emitted pause event remain after confirmed persistence. Null deletion result skips the event. Timestamp event is likewise post-write. Logging still occurs before failed persistence, preserving the original warning/error ordering.

The mock repository gains the required API. Existing automatic-pause storage-failure test invokes the updater callback before rejecting, then checks unchanged state, unpaused cron and the original warning. The filesystem stop barrier test now gates the actual writeSchedulesFile boundary reached by both APIs; original blocked-stop, persisted timestamp and restart assertions remain intact.

A one-shot spy holds writeMetadata before admission, leaving other writes able to commit. Original methods have already captured stale rows; candidate callbacks read only after the hold is released. The same test body checks pause/user edits then real stop/start. Early return/rejection before admission fails promptly without deadline polling. Other cases cover latest failure threshold, deletion, callback/identity/write failure and queue recovery.
